summary: IDS feed s100_single is degraded due to 7.7% duplicate packets (159/2059) exceeding 5% threshold. All other visibility checks healthy: bidirectional traffic present, no packet drops, no tool overload, VLANs 10,20 present, and encrypted share within tolerance for IDS.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering duplicate copies of the same packets, most likely from overlapping SPAN sessions or aggregating both sides of a TAP without deduplication. Duplicate rate 7.7% exceeds 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles and 1G port capacity processing the same packet twice, inflates flow/state tables and event counts, risks false positives and can mask true attacks, reducing detection coverage despite needing full payload and both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-level deduplication to deliver a single copy of each packet to the IDS, restoring capacity for unique traffic inspection without changing TAP/SPAN sources.
